chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hasham, the teacher, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq, and Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamdani said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hasham, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Abu Talib accepted Islam by the calculation of the camel, and he counted thirty-six with his hand. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the example of Abu Talib is like the example of the People of the Cave; they concealed faith and expressed polytheism, hence Allah gave them their reward two times.

key_terms.أَبُو طَالِب: Abu Talib, uncle of the Prophet
key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْكَهْفِ: The People of the Cave (referencing Surah Al-Kahf)
key_terms.بِحِسَابِ الْجَمَلِ: By the calculation of the camel (a method of counting)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on whether Abu Talib was a Muslim and what is the meaning of 'calculation of the camel'?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq elucidates the doctrine of 'hidden faith' (al-Ikhfa') in Abu Talib, who remained outwardly polytheistic to protect the Prophet but inwardly believed, thereby earning a double reward (ajran). The text employs the metaphor of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf) to illustrate how divine grace accommodates those who conceal their belief due to political or social necessity, a key concept in Shia theological discussions regarding the status of the Prophet's uncles.
